title: Plugin Dependencies, Artifact Contributions and Composite Mutations
description: Make mutations able to call other mutations (same artifact, other artifacts, other plugins) as one atomic undoable transaction; make plugins able to depend on other plugins (manifest dependencies, load-order graph, version requirements, dependents-aware hot reload); make plugins and extensions able to register mutations and inferences on artifacts defined by other plugins (contributions, host-side mutation router mirroring the inference router). Keep the two-tier extensibility (plugin tier + extension tier), unify the mechanisms underneath. Composite mutations are pure plans; foreign steps are driven host-side via a two-phase transaction protocol on the existing exchange channel, with parity across the Rust wasmtime host and the TypeScript browser host. Master plan: 📋️master-plan.md in this ticket folder.
summary:
Delivered the three requested mechanisms end to end, as one coherent design.

MUTATIONS CALL MUTATIONS: a composite mutation is a pure plan — `CompositeMutationKind::plan` calls other mutations through a shared `Planner`, and diff/inverse are folded from that plan (`fold_plan_diff`/`fold_plan_inverse`) rather than handwritten, so a composite cannot drift from what it composes and replay/undo/CQRS are untouched. Delegation is emitted by `#[derive(CompositeMutation)]` (a blanket impl is rejected by coherence against ~200 concrete impls). Anything touching a second artifact is host-driven: the guest returns a proposal and the host runs a two-phase transaction over the existing `exchange` channel (prepare all, commit in reverse discovery order, compensate on failure), which is the only shape that works identically in both hosts.

PLUGINS DEPEND ON PLUGINS: `PluginDependency`/`VersionReq` in the manifest, pure `resolve_load_order`/`validate_dependency_graph`/`dependents`, a `PluginGraph` in both hosts with dependency-ordered boot, dependents-aware hot reload and refused-while-depended-on unload.

CONTRIBUTIONS ACROSS PLUGINS: contribution is routing, not ownership — the owner's mutation enum stays closed; a host `ArtifactMutationRouter` (mirroring the existing inference router) resolves contributed ids, and contributed steps land in the owner's log as owner ops carrying `MutationOrigin::Contributed`, so replay never needs the contributor. Both extensibility tiers got the same machinery (`.depends_on`/`.contributes` on PluginBuilder AND ExtensionBundle; both WIT worlds export a new `contributor` interface).

VERIFIED: os-kernel 909/0, framework 137/0, plugin host 40/0, TypeScript 292/2. A shipped artifact has a real composite (flow `duplicate-widget`, planning create-widget then connect-widgets over one Planner); a shipped extension really contributes across a plugin boundary (aec-building depends_on cad, contributing one composite mutation and one inference, both refused if the dependency is removed). A composite is first-class taxonomy (`{mutation,plan}`, handwritten diff/inverse beside a plan rejected) enforced by all three validators.

NOT ACHIEVED, STATED PLAINLY: the end-to-end composite transaction over real wasm. Every plugin crate depends on semio-s-plugin-stdio, which was mid-restructure by ticket 26/08/16/FULL-STDIO-... all session and still fails to compile, so the pilots' crate gates never ran and the transaction cycle is proven against a pure-Rust harness rather than a rebuilt guest. Needs a rerun of `cargo test -p semio-s-plugin-flow` and `-p semio-s-plugin-cad-aec-building` once stdio is green. Separately, the repo's `wasm` target for semio-framework-os fails on getrandom for wasm32-unknown-unknown, keeping one TS workflow-parity test unrunnable.

PRE-EXISTING DEFECTS FOUND BY ACTUALLY RUNNING THE GATES: (1) Rust and TypeScript disagreed on the app-channel wire version (10 vs 8) with nothing reporting it — the Hello/Welcome goldens encoded the live constant, so each bump silently rewrote its own expectation; split into a codec golden plus a shared cross-language version pin. (2) A cross-language byte-identity guard had been asserting nothing since a directory restructure, and fixing its path exposed that the TS presence codec never implemented the interaction section (bit 7) Rust encodes — implemented in both directions. (3) The demonstrator's dev server never loaded the plugins it depends on. (4) Two rejection codes in the frozen taxonomy existed nowhere in code. (5) This ticket's own dependency-parity gate double-counted nested extensions.

Two read-only audits ran against the finished tree: contract conformance (73/75 conform, 0 deviate, 2 missing — both fixed) and evidence honesty (findings accepted and answered in the audit response, including one lane that wrote tests it never ran and said so).
